question:
(i) Two alternating quantities are represented by phasors rotating with the same angular frequency. Explain the meaning of phase difference between them.
(ii) If current phasor lags behind voltage phasor by $\frac{\pi}{2}$, what does it mean physically?
(iii) Why must the two phasors have the same angular frequency for a constant phase difference?

options.A:
(i) Phase difference is the difference in amplitudes of the phasors.
(ii) If current lags by $\frac{\pi}{2}$, current reaches maximum earlier than voltage.
(iii) Same frequency is not required for a constant phase difference.
options.B:
(i) Phase difference is the sum of the phasor magnitudes.
(ii) Current and voltage are in phase when current lags by $\frac{\pi}{2}$.
(iii) Different angular frequencies keep a constant angle.
options.C:
(i) Phase difference is the angle swept by one phasor in one full cycle.
(ii) Current lags by $\frac{\pi}{2}$ means current is delayed by one full cycle.
(iii) Same frequency is needed only to keep amplitudes equal.
options.D:
(i) Phase difference is the angle between phasors of the same frequency and represents time lead or lag.
(ii) If current lags voltage by $\frac{\pi}{2}$, current reaches its maximum one-fourth cycle later than voltage.
(iii) Same angular frequency is required because otherwise the angle between phasors changes continuously with time.
